paper_a.title: SAGA: A Fast Incremental Gradient Method With Support for Non-Strongly Convex Composite Objectives

paper_b.title: Accelerating Stochastic Gradient Descent using Predictive Variance Reduction

metadata.description: SAGA (paper A) directly extends SVRG (paper B) and SAG within a shared variance-reduction template $\theta_\alpha = \alpha(X-Y) + \mathbb{E}Y$. SAGA replaces SVRG's snapshot $\tilde{x}$ (refreshed only between outer epochs) with a per-sample stored gradient table updated at every step, retaining unbiasedness ($\alpha=1$, unlike SAG's biased $\alpha=1/n$) while removing the two-loop epoch structure. SAGA additionally adds support for proximal/composite objectives and a non-strongly-convex $O(n/k)$ rate not in the original SVRG paper. The proof of SAGA's Theorem 1 reuses the SVRG-style $\|a+b\|^2 \leq (1+\beta^{-1})\|a\|^2 + (1+\beta)\|b\|^2$ variance argument and the same per-component smoothness inequality (Lemma 2 here = SVRG's Eq. (8)).

matches.explanation: Both papers state the canonical finite-sum minimisation $\min \frac{1}{n}\sum_i f_i(x)$. SAGA's formulation is strictly more general: it adds a (possibly non-smooth) composite regulariser $h(x)$ with tractable proximal operator. SVRG's ProbP257.1 has only the smooth sum; the regularised SDCA-style problem appears separately as ProbP257.2. The composite extension is one of SAGA's headline contributions, so the match is analogous rather than exact.

SAGA (AP259.1) and SVRG (AP257.5) are the central algorithmic contributions of their respective papers and play the same role: variance-reduced stochastic gradient methods for finite-sum minimisation. They differ on exactly the two axes flagged in why_related: (i) SVRG uses a snapshot $\tilde{w}$ refreshed only at the start of each outer epoch (two-loop structure with explicit $\tilde\mu = \nabla P(\tilde w)$ recomputation), whereas SAGA stores a per-sample gradient table $\{f_i'(\phi_i^k)\}$ updated one entry per step (single-loop, no epochs); (ii) both estimators are unbiased (the SAG entry, which is biased, is the third method in the family). SAGA additionally supports a proximal step on $h$. The algorithms are structurally analogous templates, not the same algorithm.

SAGA cites SVRG as external prior work (AP259.6) and reproduces the SVRG update rule $x^{k+1} = x^k - \stepsize[f_j'(x^k) - f_j'(\tilde{x}) + \frac{1}{n}\sum_i f_i'(\tilde{x})]$. AP257.5 is the same SVRG algorithm in its home paper. paper-origin (B) ↔ external-origin (A) match: SAGA explicitly cites the contribution of paper B as the prior method it builds on, which is direct EXT-relation evidence.

SAGA's side-by-side update equation EP259.2 contains the SVRG line $x^{k+1} = x^k - \stepsize[f_j'(x^k) - f_j'(\tilde{x}) + \frac{1}{n}\sum_i f_i'(\tilde{x})]$ verbatim, modulo notation ($\tilde{x}$ vs $\tilde{w}$, $\stepsize$ vs $\eta_t$). EP257.3 is the same equation in its home paper. Exact match up to notation.

SAGA's RP259.1 explicitly positions SAGA as the variance-reduction midpoint between SAG and SVRG, identifying SVRG's choice as $\alpha = 1$ with $Y = f_j'(\tilde{x})$ updated only between outer loops. The corresponding content in SVRG is split across three remarks: RP257.2 (unbiasedness of the SVRG update, matching $\alpha = 1$), RP257.3 (control-variate/auxiliary-function derivation), and RP257.4 (variance vanishes at the optimum, the empirical motivation for variance reduction). SAGA's remark unifies and extends this commentary by also placing SAG and SAGA in the same picture.

Both papers cite the same external method, SAG (Le Roux/Schmidt/Bach, 2012), for the same purpose: a biased variance-reduced stochastic gradient method that motivates the SVRG/SAGA family. external ↔ external match; per the spec, this carries no information for the pair-level relation_type but is recorded for completeness.

Both papers cite SDCA (Shalev-Shwartz & Zhang) as external prior work and present essentially the same dual-coordinate-ascent algorithm. external ↔ external match; carries no signal for relation_type.

Both are the main convergence theorems of their respective papers, asserting linear/geometric contraction in the smooth strongly-convex setting. SVRG's TP257.1 gives $\mathbb{E}P(\tilde w_s) - P(w^*) \leq \alpha^s [P(\tilde w_0) - P(w^*)]$ with $\alpha = \frac{1}{\gamma\eta(1-2L\eta)m} + \frac{2L\eta}{1-2L\eta}$, a per-epoch contraction in function value. SAGA's TP259.1 gives a per-step Lyapunov contraction $\mathbb{E}[T^{k+1}] \leq (1 - 1/\kappa) T^k$ with $\kappa = 2(\mu n + L)/\mu$; CP259.1 turns this into $\mathbb{E}\|x^k - x^*\|^2 \leq (1 - \frac{\mu}{2(\mu n + L)})^k [\dots]$, a per-step contraction in iterate distance. Same conceptual claim (linear convergence under smoothness + strong convexity), but the rate constants and even the metric (function value vs distance vs Lyapunov) differ. SAGA's bound is per-step rather than per-epoch, reflecting the absence of an outer loop.

SAGA's Lemma 2 is the per-component version evaluated at table points $\phi_i$ rather than a common $w$, but the underlying smoothness identity (and proof) match exactly. Cross-type (lemma+proof ↔ proof_step) but the mathematical content corresponds directly.

SAGA's Lemma 3 (LP259.3) bounds $\mathbb{E}\|w^{k+1} - x^k - \stepsize f'(x^*)\|^2$ using the tighter inequality $\|x+y\|^2 \leq (1 + \beta^{-1})\|x\|^2 + (1+\beta)\|y\|^2$ together with $\mathbb{E}\|X - \mathbb{E}X\|^2 \leq \mathbb{E}\|X\|^2$; PP259.6 explicitly states this 'mirrors the SVRG variance argument'. SVRG's PSP257.4 bounds $\mathbb{E}\|v_t\|^2$ using exactly $\|a+b\|^2 \leq 2\|a\|^2 + 2\|b\|^2$ (the $\beta = 1$ specialisation) and $\mathbb{E}\|\xi - \mathbb{E}\xi\|^2 \leq \mathbb{E}\|\xi\|^2$, then combines with Eq. (8). Same proof template, with SAGA generalising the constant from $\beta = 1$ to a tunable $\beta > 0$ (needed because the SAGA convergence proof selects $\beta = (2\mu n + L)/L$). Cross-type (lemma+proof ↔ proof_step) but the structural correspondence is direct.

Composite L1+L2 alignment of the two main convergence proofs. Both proofs share the variance-reduction backbone: bound $\mathbb{E}\|\text{stochastic-step}\|^2$ via $\|a+b\|^2 \leq (1+\beta^{-1})\|a\|^2 + (1+\beta)\|b\|^2$ + per-component smoothness (PSP259.4 uses LP259.3 ↔ PSP257.4); expand $\mathbb{E}\|x^{k+1} - x^*\|^2$ (PSP259.3 ↔ PSP257.5); apply strong convexity to absorb cross-terms and conclude (PSP259.5/PSP259.6 ↔ PSP257.6/PSP257.7). SAGA's proof differs structurally because it tracks a Lyapunov function $T^k$ that includes the gradient-table state (PSP259.1, PSP259.2 have no SVRG counterpart since SVRG has no per-step table), and operates per-step rather than per-epoch (no SVRG-style summation over $t = 1, \dots, m$). SVRG's PSP257.6 explicitly sums over the inner loop $m$, which has no analog in SAGA. Confidence medium because the granularities and Lyapunov choices differ enough that step-by-step pairing is approximate.

SAGA's Lemma 1 (LP259.1) is the strong-convexity inner-product bound $\langle f'(x), x^* - x\rangle \leq \frac{L-\mu}{L}[f(x^*) - f(x)] - \frac{\mu}{2}\|x^* - x\|^2 - \frac{1}{2Ln}\sum_i \|f_i'(x^*) - f_i'(x)\|^2 - \frac{\mu}{L}\langle f'(x^*), x - x^*\rangle$, with proof PP259.4 (apply LP259.4 with $y = x^*$, average over $f_i$). This is a refined/co-coercivity-type inequality used to absorb cross-terms in the SAGA Lyapunov proof. SVRG's proof does not need this bound because its analysis works per-epoch on function values rather than per-step on a Lyapunov potential.

SAGA's Lemma A1 (LP259.4) is the strong-convexity lower bound $f(x) \geq f(y) + \langle f'(y), x-y\rangle + \frac{1}{2(L-\mu)}\|f'(x)-f'(y)\|^2 + \dots$, used to derive Lemma 1. PP259.3 is its proof (define $g(x) = f(x) - \frac{\mu}{2}\|x\|^2$, apply standard convex inequality, substitute back). SVRG's analysis does not need this auxiliary bound or its proof.

The Lyapunov potential $T^k = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i f_i(\phi_i^k) - f(x^*) - \frac{1}{n}\sum_i \langle f_i'(x^*), \phi_i^k - x^*\rangle + c\|x^k - x^*\|^2$ is specific to SAGA: it explicitly tracks the per-sample gradient-table state $\{\phi_i^k\}$ alongside the iterate. SVRG has no per-sample table and consequently no analog Lyapunov function; it proves convergence directly on function value $P(\tilde w_s) - P(w^*)$.

SAGA defines the proximal operator $\mathrm{prox}^h_\stepsize(y) = \arg\min_x\{h(x) + \frac{1}{2\stepsize}\|x - y\|^2\}$ to support composite objectives with non-smooth $h$. SVRG (paper B) does not handle composite objectives in its main algorithm and never defines a prox; this is part of the EXT contribution from B to A.

The SAGA-specific update equation $w^{k+1} = x^k - \stepsize[f_j'(\phi_j^{k+1}) - f_j'(\phi_j^k) + \frac{1}{n}\sum_i f_i'(\phi_i^k)]$ has no SVRG analog because SVRG uses the snapshot $\tilde x$ in place of $\phi_j$ (the SVRG version is captured separately in EP257.3 and matched above).
Finito/MISO update equation; Finito-family methods are SAGA-paper context that does not appear in the SVRG paper.
Equivalent $u$-form reformulation of SAGA exposing the link to Finito/MISO; no SVRG counterpart.
Primal reformulation of SDCA via Moreau decomposition; SVRG-paper has SDCA only as cited external work (AP257.4) and does not derive a primal version.
SDCA/Finito midpoint variant introduced in SAGA's appendix; no SVRG counterpart.
Finito/MISO is cited by SAGA as related variance-reduced work; not cited or discussed in the SVRG paper.

SAGA's $O(n/k)$ rate for the non-strongly-convex case (Theorem 2 plus its proof and step decomposition) is a SAGA-paper contribution with no SVRG counterpart in this extraction. SVRG mentions a non-strongly-convex extension in passing (RP257.6) but has no theorem or proof, so we do not match the contributions. The proof itself uses an 'augmented Lyapunov function' approach plus a 'prox-SVRG inequality', which references Xiao & Zhang's prox-SVRG paper rather than the original SVRG paper being aligned here.

SVRG's generalised stochastic gradient framework $w^{(t)} = w^{(t-1)} - \eta_t g_t(w^{(t-1)}, \xi_t)$ with $\mathbb{E}[g_t \mid w^{(t-1)}] = \nabla P(w^{(t-1)})$ is a high-level setup equation. SAGA does not state this framework explicitly, though its DP259.3 (control-variate $\theta_\alpha$) plays a related framing role and is matched separately. Marked none rather than analogous because EP257.1 is at a level of generality that SAGA doesn't reproduce.

$L$-smoothness definition. SAGA uses the same property as an assumption in LP259.1, LP259.2, LP259.4 but does not lift it to a standalone definition node. No L1 paper-origin definition in SAGA matches it.
$\gamma$-strong convexity definition. As with smoothness, SAGA uses strong convexity as an assumption in TP259.1 etc. but has no standalone definition node.

SVRG's snapshot average gradient $\tilde\mu = \nabla P(\tilde w) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i \nabla\psi_i(\tilde w)$ is precisely the SVRG-specific quantity SAGA replaces with a per-step running table. No SAGA equation node corresponds; the snapshot is the structural feature SAGA removes.

SVRG's Section 4 SDCA-as-variance-reduction discussion (regularised problem ProbP257.2, dual representation EP257.4, dual update EP257.5, and remark RP257.7 framing SDCA as a variance-reduction method) is an aside in the SVRG paper. SAGA discusses SDCA from a different angle (primal reformulation AP259.3, midpoint variant AP259.4) and the contents do not pair cleanly. Listed none collectively for compactness.

SVRG's RP257.1 contrasts SGD's $O(1/t)$ rate with GD's $O((1 - \gamma/L)^t)$ linear rate, motivating variance reduction. SAGA does not include an analogous standalone remark; the comparison is implicit in the convergence-rate table of the introduction (which the extraction did not lift to a remark node).

SAGA-specific 'adaptivity to strong convexity' remark: with $\stepsize = 1/(3L)$, SAGA automatically achieves rate $(1 - \min\{1/(4n), \mu/(3L)\})^k$ without retuning. SVRG has no analog: its convergence theorem requires $\eta$ to be tuned with knowledge of $\gamma$, and it has no claim of $\mu$-adaptivity.

SAGA's storage-trick remark (one scalar per sample for linear predictors) is an implementation contribution unique to SAGA. SVRG does not need such a trick because it stores only the snapshot $\tilde w$ and $\tilde\mu$, not a per-sample table.
Just-in-time updating for sparse gradients; a SAGA implementation note inherited from SAG. SVRG paper does not discuss sparse updates.
Explicit-quadratic-regulariser variant of SAGA; SAGA-specific implementation detail with no SVRG counterpart.
